claims.text: The alloy has a dual-phase microstructure comprising a disordered FCC matrix and ordered B2 precipitates.
The initial alloy has random or only short-range chemical ordering.
Intermediate aging at approximately 400–700 °C induces increased long-range order in the B2 phase.
Intermediate aging forms LCO clusters at FCC/B2 phase boundaries.
The proposed aging treatment does not cause significant grain coarsening or impurity segregation.
Brittleness is produced when ordered B2 domains and coherent, high-energy LCO boundaries percolate.
The transient transition is not caused by grain-boundary embrittlement.
The phase boundaries become coherent and compositionally modulated during intermediate aging.
Increased local chemical order raises the energy barrier for dislocation cross-slip because dislocation motion must break ordered bonds.
Suppression of cross-slip forces dislocations into planar slip.
Planar slip causes localized strain accumulation and shear-band formation.
Localized strain and shear bands cause the transient loss of ductility.
At higher aging temperatures, LCO relaxes or B2 domains coarsen.
LCO relaxation or B2-domain coarsening reduces the cross-slip barrier and restores ductility.
The brittleness maximum coincides with the maximum density of coherent LCO boundaries and the minimum cross-slip rate.
Low-temperature aging produces no significant LCO evolution, whereas high-temperature aging produces LCO relaxation or coarsening.
Impurity-segregation-driven grain-boundary embrittlement would produce continuous embrittlement without high-temperature recovery.
The embrittlement regime occurs after coherent LCO-bearing interfaces percolate but before they coarsen significantly.
The B2 phase is the primary site of consequential LCO evolution, while LCO in the FCC phase is negligible.
Intergranular versus transgranular fracture morphology can discriminate grain-boundary embrittlement from the proposed LCO/phase-boundary mechanism.

contradictions.description: The initial B2 precipitates are described as ordered while the same initial state is also described as having random or only short-range chemical ordering. This is inconsistent if the latter characterization is intended to include the B2 phase rather than only the FCC matrix.
